info.title: Grid wire contract
info.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 contract for the grid daemon (crates/wire is the Rust source of truth; this document is the normative external vocabulary). Conventions: (1) Promise-space vs actual-space — a Plan (promised delta) references code by CallsignPattern because unwritten code has no Datum yet; a Diff (actual delta) is datum-space with callsign annotations; the gate verdict unifies the two. This is wire epoch 1: the one declared break, taken before any consumer existed (docs/plans/2026-09-01-naming.md); epoch 0 is served by nothing. (2) Grade ranking, strongest first: proven (compiler-grade static) > observed (happened in a trace at least once) > modeled (registry/schema unification) > heuristic (name/shape match). Filters use at_or_above semantics. (3) Fuel exhaustion is not an error: a walk that runs out of fuel returns status 'aground' with its frontier, and the caller may resume. (4) Determinism: for a given snapshot_id, pure query methods return identical results across calls and daemon restarts, with two carve-outs: the stats object is excluded from the comparison surface, and walks that set fuel.max_ms are excluded entirely, since wall-clock exhaustion varies run to run. The C2 property test compares responses with stats stripped and max_ms unset; callers wanting cacheable results budget by max_hops/max_nodes only. (5) Versioning: this document is semver'd; breaking changes bump major; the daemon reports its wire version via grid.version and refuses clients that pin an incompatible major.

x-transport.framing: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0; requests may pipeline; responses correlate by id
x-transport.config_prefix: All env vars and config keys use GRID_ / grid. prefixes

x-porcelain.description: Normative grammar for human-facing stdout records. --json emits wire results verbatim; the porcelain version is reported by grid.version.

methods.name: grid.version
methods.summary: Report wire and engine versions plus the current snapshot, if any.

porcelain.description: Porcelain grammar semver; normative in docs/PORCELAIN.md

methods.name: grid.snapshot.current
methods.summary: Return the currently published snapshot.

methods.name: grid.survey.run
methods.summary: Run a survey of the repo (or a specific rev/worktree) and publish a new snapshot. Incremental by content hash; idempotent for an unchanged tree.

schema.description: Absolute path to a worktree to survey instead of the daemon's default repo

methods.name: grid.resolve
methods.summary: Resolve a locator (datum, position, callsign, or file:line) to definition references. Unknown locators resolve to an empty list, not an error.

methods.name: grid.delta
methods.summary: Compute the actual delta (Diff) between two snapshots or revs. Datum set-difference plus edge changes with move detection.

methods.name: grid.gate.check
methods.summary: Check a Plan (promised delta + expected tests + invariants) against the Diff at head. The verdict feeds the Buildhost merge-gate pipeline.

invariants.description: Board code may not call persistence directly

methods.name: grid.query.walk
methods.summary: Run a walk walk: budgeted, evidence-filtered multi-hop traversal. Reachability sweep when 'to' is absent; path-finding when present.

methods.name: grid.anchor.carry
methods.summary: Carry anchors forward to a target snapshot along the patch DAG. Never errors per-anchor: unresolvable anchors come back status 'orphaned'.

examples.name: carry a review pin across an edit

methods.name: grid.trace.ingest
methods.summary: Ingest a trace (runtime trace from a test run). Observations are resolved to datums where possible; unresolved symbols are returned, not dropped silently.

methods.name: grid.cache.check
methods.summary: Look up stored verification verdicts. Hits return the recorded verdict (pass or fail) for an identical per-kind key; misses mean run it and record via grid.cache.record.

examples.name: check verdict cache before running tests

methods.name: grid.cache.record
methods.summary: Record verification verdicts, populating the cache that grid.cache.check reads. Grid freezes each entry's per-kind closure key at record time; definitions whose closure cannot be fully established are rejected, not stored.

schema.description: Trace produced by the recorded run, if any; stored on each entry.

rejected.description: Entries grid refused to store, e.g. closure unresolved or fuel-exhausted at key-freeze time. Rejection is the record-side face of one-directional soundness.

previous.description: The verdict the same key already held.

nondeterministic.description: Entries whose key already held the opposite verdict: same closure, same environment, a different answer. The closure proves the charted code did not change, so the claim is exactly "not the charted code" — a race is code, and grid does not say flake. Detected from the last entry at record time; the new verdict is stored regardless.

methods.name: grid.scope
methods.summary: Context pack for a planned edit: signatures and handles (not bodies), edges in and out, in-scope invariants, open anchors, churn. Token cost proportional to blast radius.

methods.name: grid.plan.lint
methods.summary: Validate a plan before code exists: promised callsigns must resolve or plausibly pattern-match; promised edges are checked against standing invariants. Pure validation — no survey.

examples.name: impossible plan dies at plan time

methods.name: grid.plan.estimate
methods.summary: Blast radius as numbers: definitions in the promised delta's closure, tests in reverse closure, predicted cache misses. Mechanical footing for effort estimation.

methods.name: grid.edit.apply
methods.summary: The only write path besides survey. Coordinate-addressed edits with compare-and-swap: base_datum must equal the current datum or the edit conflicts; absent base_datum means creation (target must not exist) — grid's own config bootstrap uses this path, there is no separate init write. Daemon-serialized.

methods.name: grid.todo
methods.summary: A view over grid.gate.check's promise accounting — not a second delta engine. The plan's promises partitioned into done and pending, with a fraction over all promise kinds.

methods.name: grid.check
methods.summary: Is this change ok, in one call: the gate verdict, and why — per-promise fulfilling paths, surplus with provenance, changed-but-unexecuted coverage, open anchors.

methods.name: grid.trace.diff
methods.summary: Two traces compared at call granularity; the first divergent hop is where behavior forked. Requires trace retention.

methods.name: grid.suspects
methods.summary: Fault localization: the failing test's observed closure intersected with the recent delta, ranked. Requires trace retention and a populated verdict cache for history-aware scoring.

examples.name: rank suspects for a red test

ranked.via: changed in delta and observed in failing trace

methods.name: grid.bisect
methods.summary: Bisect over the patch DAG, accelerated by the verdict cache: each probe re-runs only tests whose closure changed. Requires a populated cache.

methods.name: grid.drift
methods.summary: Dependents of changed interfaces: definitions that depend on something whose sig moved, and that did not themselves change. The set the compiler cannot enumerate across languages, re-exports and processes.

schema.description: Also enumerate every known test and report the ones whose recorded verdict no longer applies.

methods.name: grid.test.plan
methods.summary: Test selection as data, no running: which of the runner's tests a change can reach, which recorded verdicts still apply, and which changed definitions no test reaches. The CLI spawns the runner and records verdicts through grid.cache.record; the daemon only answers the plan.

params.name: base
params.description: Absent means the last snapshot a `grid test` recorded against, else HEAD.

schema.description: The environment the run would happen in; a replayed verdict must have been recorded under the same one.
The runner's own inventory. Grid never guesses what a test is.
Absent or true: an unselected test's verdict is looked up and replayed. False: nothing is looked up, and every unselected test is selected as not_recorded.

examples.name: select tests for an uncommitted edit

Datum.description: Definition identity: blake3 of the normalized AST (alpha-renamed locals; formatting and comments excluded). The reference all coordinates are measured from.

SnapshotId.description: Content-derived snapshot identity: blake3 of the canonical segment manifest the survey produced — never a minted id. A clean tree's snapshot is a pure function of (rev, segment-format epoch); a dirty tree folds in the worktree diff hash. Idempotent by construction: re-surveying an identical state returns the same id, and identical states dedupe to one snapshot. Porcelain displays @rev or @rev+tree, never this raw form. All segment writes are serialized through the daemon (single writer); the CLI never writes segments directly.

GitRev.description: Git commit SHA, abbreviated or full.

SnapshotOrRev.description: A published snapshot, or a git rev the daemon will survey on demand.

Lang.description: Language adapter that produced a definition.

role.description: Structural role within the parent node, language-scoped: e.g. 'param', 'body', 'stmt', 'call', 'arm', 'field'.

index.description: Ordinal among siblings sharing the role.

AstPath.description: Interior coordinate: structural path inside a definition's AST, by role, never by byte offset. Empty array addresses the whole definition.

Position.description: An exact position in code: a datum plus an optional interior path.

Callsign.description: Fully qualified human name, dot-separated, e.g. 'cortana.reaper.TagContract.validate'. Mutable: a rename rebinds the callsign, the datum does not change.

CallsignPattern.description: Glob over callsigns: '*' matches one segment, '**' matches any number, e.g. 'cortana.reaper.**'. Promise-space references use patterns because unwritten code has no datum.

Handle.description: Input convenience: callsign plus a datum-prefix disambiguator, e.g. 'cortana.reaper.TagContract.validate@9f2c'. The prefix must resolve uniquely within the snapshot (git short-SHA auto-lengthening). Display default is the bare callsign; results keep full datums — handles are for input and for renders where identity beyond the name matters.

oneOf.description: Advisory: resolves via the current materialization; prefer datum or callsign.

Locator.description: Any way of pointing at code. Exactly one variant.

signature.description: One-line declaration as surveyed, e.g. 'def validate(self, tags: list[Tag]) -> Receipt'. Lets grid.scope return signatures without bodies.

materialization.description: Advisory only: where the definition currently happens to live. Files are projections; never store this as an address.

Relation.description: Typed edge kinds of the chart. The call graph is the 'calls' + 'dispatches_to' view.

Grade.description: Evidence grade (after CATZOC), listed strongest first: proven = compiler-grade static; observed = seen in a trace at least once; modeled = registry/schema/route unification; heuristic = name or shape match. Filters use at_or_above semantics over this order.

via.description: For modeled edges, the bridge that established the connection, e.g. 'route:/api/cards/:id' or 'key:card.archived'.

Edit.description: One edit edge in the patch DAG (the log): a definition's predecessor and successor identities.

worktree_diff_hash.description: Present iff the surveyed tree was dirty: blake3 of the canonical worktree diff vs git_rev. Porcelain renders @rev+<prefix>.

declined.description: What the survey declined to bind, split by why. Absent from a snapshot nobody re-surveyed in this run, so an unknown count is never reported as zero. The three add up to the survey's declined total.

external.description: Names that were never this tree's to hold — std/core/alloc or another crate in Rust, a top-level module the tree does not root in Python.

method.description: Calls through a receiver whose type would have to be known. Counted, never resolved.

internal.description: Names this tree could have held and the resolver could not bind: glob-supplied, ambiguous, an unresolved re-export. The hole.

moved_from.description: For action 'moved': the callsign the datum answered to before. A rename rebinds the callsign; the datum does not change.

sig_changed.description: Whether the interface identity changed, when both snapshots carry sigs. Absent means at least one side predates segment epoch 3, and a consumer treats unknown as changed.

DefChange.description: added: 'after' only. removed: 'before' only. modified: both (this pair is a Edit).

moved_from.description: Present iff action is 'moved': the edge's previous endpoints. A move is not a remove+add.

Diff.description: The actual delta, datum-space. Deterministically ordered: defs by callsign, edges by (relation, src, dst).

PlanDelta.description: The promised delta, name-space (patterns), authored by the planner before code exists.

test.description: Test node id as the runner reports it, e.g. 'tests/test_tag_contract.py::test_retry_window'.

new.description: True if the plan promises this test does not exist at base.

EdgeRule.description: Edge shape for invariants. Omitted relation means any. at_or_above defaults to 'heuristic' (i.e. any evidence).

Invariant.description: A standing query checked at every gate, e.g. forbid_edge {src: 'cortana.boards.**', relation: 'calls', dst: 'cortana.persistence.**'} — board code may not call persistence directly. The pattern language has no negation; state rules in positive scope terms.

plan_rev.description: Plan revision this plan was authored against, e.g. 'v3'.

tolerate.description: Surplus edge changes matching any rule here do not hold the gate; they surface in GateVerdict.tolerated. The pressure valve against gate fatigue from incidental helper edges.

Plan.description: The spec: promised delta + expected test outcomes + invariants + tolerances. Authored by the planner; checked by grid.gate.check.

InvariantViolation.description: The witness path is the concrete evidence chain that violates the invariant.

surplus.description: Made good, not promised, and not tolerated.

tolerated.description: Surplus changes matched by Plan.tolerate; reported for visibility, never a hold cause.

defs_unaccounted.description: Definitions changed by the diff but covered by no def promise.

reasons.description: Human-readable one-liners, one per contributing hold cause; empty on pass.

GateVerdict.description: Cross-plan error. Surplus is computed after tolerate filtering. gate is 'hold' iff missing, surplus, defs_unaccounted, a failed TestComparison, or an invariant violation is non-empty; 'pass' otherwise. The verdict itemizes divergence — it never says only 'hold'.

max_ms.description: Optional wall-clock guard, deliberately no default. Unlike hop/node budgets it is nondeterministic: results truncated by max_ms are outside the determinism claim. Leave unset for cacheable results.

Fuel.description: Traversal budget. Every walk carries fuel; there are no unbounded queries.

to.description: Present: find paths from 'from' to 'to'. Absent: reachability sweep from 'from'.

relations.description: Restrict traversal to these edge kinds. Absent means all.

Path.description: edges[i] connects nodes[i] to nodes[i+1]; edges.length = nodes.length - 1. Every hop carries its grade — a path's overall confidence is its weakest hop.

frontier.description: Present iff status is 'aground': where the walk ran out of fuel. Resume by issuing a new walk from the frontier.

WalkStats.description: Diagnostics, plus one claim. visited/hops/ms are diagnostics and are excluded from the determinism comparison surface; complete_within is not a diagnostic — it is a statement about the answer, is a pure function of the graph and the query, and belongs to the comparison surface.

complete_within.description: Depth through which the answer is complete: every definition reachable within this many hops, under this query's relations and evidence floor, is in the result. On 'complete' it is the effective hop bound. On 'aground' it is the last layer the walk fully expanded before the budget refused; absent when even the roots' own layer did not finish, which certifies nothing and says so.

anchor_id.description: Storage identity only; renders display the anchor's position handle, never the ULID.

Anchor.description: A durable reference into code, owned by a consumer (e.g. an Artifacts review annotation). Grid stores no annotation payloads — only positions.

status.description: exact: datum unchanged. carried: followed edits to a successor. orphaned: no successor found; 'position' is absent.

via.description: The edits followed, in order; empty when exact.

symbol.description: Raw runtime symbol when the instrument cannot know datums, e.g. 'cortana/reaper.py:TagContract.validate'. The daemon resolves it.

trace_id.description: Storage identity only; renders display the contextual form command@rev/time, never the ULID.

command.description: The test command that produced this trace.

snapshot.description: The chart snapshot this trace's observations were mapped against, set by the coverage ingestion paths (--lcov, --coverage-json). It pins the chart a later reader must grade the trace against without resolving git_rev through git, which a shallow clone or a rewritten history can no longer answer. Absent on a trace a runner emitted directly, where git_rev is all there is.

Trace.description: A runtime trace from a test run: the path actually traveled. Ingested observations become grade 'observed' edges.

env_hash.description: Caller-computed hash of every verification input not reachable through the chart: toolchain, flags, config files (tsconfig, lint rules), fixtures, golden files, migrations, env vars. The caller warrants its completeness.

snapshot.description: Chart snapshot the closures are computed against. Absent means the current published snapshot; the resolved id is echoed in the result. Closures are a function of the chart, so the chart is part of the key.

CacheCheckRequest.description: Cache lookup. Keys are per-kind, all scoped by (env_hash, snapshot). lint keys on span_hash — blake3 of the definition's raw source bytes at the snapshot — because comments (noqa, eslint-disable) are lint input that the normalized datum deliberately discards. typecheck keys on span_hash plus the closure over proven signature-bearing edges (type-ignore comments are self-input; dependency signatures live in their datums). test keys on the closure over ALL edges regardless of grade — closure traversal ignores at_or_above by design, since a missed dependency is a false hit. Soundness is one-directional: a miss for a cacheable definition is acceptable; a hit for a closure grid could not fully establish is a contract violation. What the chart cannot see — hermeticity, ambient state, monkeypatching — is warranted by the caller, not by grid (assurance claim C4).

verdict.description: The stored result. fail-hits are the valuable case: skip re-running a known-red verification.

trace_id.description: Present when the recorded run also produced a trace.

test.description: Present when the hit was looked up for a named test (grid.test.plan): the test whose verdict this is.

snapshot.description: The snapshot the closures were computed against.

CacheCheckResult.description: {hit.datum} ∪ misses = request.datums, disjoint. Normative: any datum whose closure traversal exhausted fuel or touched an unresolved endpoint is a miss — never a hit.

PlanId.description: Plan identity, resolved against the daemon's plan store (.grid/plans).

TraceId.description: Trace storage identity (ULID); renders display command@rev/time.

defs.description: Signatures ride on DefRef.signature; bodies are fetched separately and deliberately absent.

invariants.description: Standing invariants whose scope patterns intersect the requested callsigns.

churn.description: Edit-frequency signal: edit count per definition in scope.

promise.description: Canonical rendering of the offending promise.

LintResult.description: Pure validation of a plan — no survey, no snapshot involved.

target.description: Callsign, or callsign@prefix handle. Creation edits (no base_datum) use a bare callsign.

base_datum.description: CAS guard: present — the current datum must equal it, or the edit conflicts. Absent — creation: the target must not exist. Grid's own config bootstrap is a creation edit; there is no separate init write path.

was.description: The stale base_datum; absent for creation conflicts (target already exists).

EditResult.description: Conflicts are data, not errors: the caller re-reads and retries with fresh coordinates.

fraction.description: Over all promise kinds: defs + edges + tests.

CheckResult.description: Is this change ok: the gate verdict, and the reasoning behind it. The verdict is grid.gate.check's own, so a reviewer and CI cannot disagree about whether the promise was kept.

coverage.description: Changed but not reached by the supplied trace — the reviewer's red flags.

CheckWhy.description: Why the verdict says what it says: a path per fulfilled promise, the surplus nobody promised, what changed without being run, and what is still open against this code.

first_divergence.description: Absent when the traces are identical.

via.description: Why this ranked: the intersection that implicated it.
The boundary the coupling crosses: 'schema', 'wire', 'protocol' — free text, and the word that appears in a drift record's reason.

Covenant.description: A declared, symmetric coupling between two callsign patterns that no language's binding rules establish — a serde boundary, a JSON contract, a Python dict a Rust struct deserializes. A human knows the pair; this is where it is written down. Declared coupling is the one modeled evidence that gates, because a human declared it.

def.description: The definition whose behaviour moved while this test kept passing, as it was at base.

WeakTest.description: A test that covered a definition, kept passing while that definition's body changed, and was not itself touched — so it proved nothing about the change. Heuristic: a ranking, never a gate.

reason.description: closure-changed: the recorded verdict keys to a closure this snapshot no longer has. closure-rejected: the closure could not be established at all, which is a miss and therefore never a hit.

StaleTest.description: A test whose recorded verdict no longer applies. Staleness is identity math over the closure, not a guess, so it gates.

weight.description: +1 the suspect appeared, -1 it was retracted. A retraction is emitted when an edit resolves a suspect — the dependent was updated, a covenant was satisfied, the interface was reverted. Consumers hold a running sum, and the sum after any prefix of events equals a fresh grid drift.

DriftDelta.description: One signed change to the suspect set. Watch mode emits these rather than a current list, so a consumer never has to diff lists to see what changed, and the algebra of the stream is checkable by summation.

subject.description: The callsign or pattern the warning is about.

dependent.description: The definition that depends on the changed one and did not itself change.

changed.description: The definition whose interface moved, as it was at base.

grade.description: Evidence grade of the edge that made this a suspect.

sig_before.description: The changed definition's interface identity at base, when the snapshot carries one.

sig_after.description: Its interface identity at head, when the snapshot carries one. Absent on both sides means the sig was unknown and the change was treated as visible.

reason.description: Why this edge implicated the dependent beyond the edge itself: 'stale-trace' for a decayed observation, 'covenant:<via>' for a declared coupling.

unresolved_refs.description: References the head survey declined to bind, so no edge exists for them and no dependent could be found through them. Absent means head was a published snapshot nobody re-surveyed in this run, so the count is unknown — never reported as zero.

unresolved_external.description: Of unresolved_refs: names that were never this tree's to hold — std/core/alloc or another crate in Rust, a top-level module the tree does not root in Python. They cost a claim about this repo nothing. Absent whenever unresolved_refs is.

unresolved_method.description: Of unresolved_refs: calls through a receiver whose type would have to be known. Never resolved and never guessed, because types are modeled and a survey emits none. Absent whenever unresolved_refs is.

unresolved_internal.description: Of unresolved_refs: names this tree could have held and the resolver could not bind — glob-supplied, ambiguous, an unresolved re-export. The population that is an actual hole in what drift claims. Absent whenever unresolved_refs is.

budget_rejected.description: Definitions whose inbound walk ran past its budget. The walk is rejected whole, never truncated: a truncated walk is indistinguishable from a smaller one.

unattributed_entries.description: Recorded verdicts no retained trace claims, so no test owns them and no test-staleness check covered them. Present when the report was asked for tests.

weak_skipped.description: Weak-test checks declined because their coverage came from a decayed trace. A heuristic built on a demoted heuristic is noise, so grid declines it and says how often.

DriftUnchecked.description: What drift could not check. A drift report claiming no suspects where it could not see callers is dishonest silence, so the counts ride with every answer.

warnings.description: Reported rather than refused: a declared covenant whose pattern matches nothing at drift time, and anything else drift wants a human to see without holding on it.

stale_tests.description: Present when the report was asked for tests: every known test whose recorded verdict no longer applies.

weak.description: Present when the report was asked for tests: tests that covered a changed definition, stayed green, and were never touched. Ranked, never gated.

culprit.description: Absent when the range is clean or the culprit is outside surveyed code.

TestId.description: A test as the runner names it, never as grid guesses it: nextest's `<binary-id> <name>` (`pkg::bin/x mod::tests::t`), pytest's node id (`tests/test_x.py::TestY::test_z`). Grid maps it to a callsign by the frontend's spelling and resolves it by the grid.resolve rule; a test the chart cannot resolve is always run.

datum.description: The test's definition at head. Absent when the test is unresolved.

why.description: reached: the inbound walk from the changed set reached the test's definition (or the test itself changed). no_trace: no retained trace still describes code base holds, so the static closure alone may not excuse a skip. unresolved: the chart cannot name the test, so nothing can be said about it. aground: the walk ran out of fuel, so every test is selected. not_recorded: unreached and traced, but no verdict for this closure in this environment is on record to replay.

TestSelection.description: One test the runner must run, and the reason. Every reason is a refusal to skip.

head.description: The worktree survey the plan was computed against.

selected.description: The run set: selected ∪ replayed = the inventory, disjoint.

replayed.description: Unselected tests whose recorded verdict, keyed by the closure at head and the given environment, is on record. Each hit names its test.

uncovered.description: Changed definitions the walk connected to no test. Heuristic: the chart is known incomplete, so this ranks and never gates.

TestPlan.description: Selection as data: one inbound walk from the datum-level changed set over every grade, fuel grid_cache::FUEL. A walk that runs aground selects every test rather than a shorter list; a test with no live trace is selected regardless of the walk.

trace_id.description: Present when the run was traced and the trace was ingested.

env_hash.description: blake3 over toolchain version, lockfile bytes, runner args, target triple, and whether the run was traced — stated so a verdict can be re-keyed later.

ran.description: What the runner said about each selected test it reported on.

warnings.description: nondeterministic and uncovered findings. Reported, never gated.

TestRun.description: What `grid test --json` emits. No method answers it: the run is the CLI's, the way a survey's git spawn is; the plan inside it is grid.test.plan's answer verbatim.

NoSnapshot.message: no snapshot published yet; run grid.survey.run

CorruptSegment.message: segment failed validation on load; store integrity is suspect
